newsitem.title: USA: New Yorkers stream into marriage offices.
newsitem.headline: New Yorkers stream into marriage offices.

text.p: New Yorkers are crowding the corridors of city marriage offices, but officials are not sure whether it is romance or immigrants rushing to wed U.S. citizens because they fear deportation under a new immigration law.
City officials said that on Tuesday and Wednesday, fights even broke out among couples who had been waiting for hours to collect marriage licenses or to be joined in brief marriage ceremonies.
"In my 11 years here this is the biggest increase in marriages I've ever seen," said New York City Clerk Carlos Cuevas, head of the city's five marriage bureaux.

He said the trend started last month with 2,109 weddings in Manhattan -- an increase of 88 percent in marriage performed compared with January 1996. The increase in the borough of Queens was 118 percent, he said.
Immigration advocates said the surge in marriages was partly due to a new federal immigration law containing rules that could lead to deportations or loss of benefits for many immigrants.
The law passed by Congress last year takes effect on April 1, but is not expected to lead to mass deportations.
The immigration advocates said that ironically, marrying may not be the solution many immigrants are looking for -- marriage does not automatically confer citizenship.
Under the new law, marriage provides only the right to apply for legal residency, a process that can take years.
